text: FCFeynmanProjectivize[int, x] checks if the given Feynman parameter integral (without prefactors) depending on x[1], x[2], … is a projective form. If this is not the case, the integral will be projectivized.
Projectivity is a necessary condition for computing the integral with the aid of the Cheng-Wu theorem
int = SFAD[{p3, mg^2}] SFAD[{p3 - p1, mg^2}] SFAD[{{0, -2 p1 . q}}]

fp = FCFeynmanParametrize[int, {p1, p3}, Names -> x, Indexed -> True, FCReplaceD -> {D -> 4 - 2 ep}, Simplify -> True, Assumptions -> {mg > 0, ep > 0}, FinalSubstitutions -> {SPD[q] -> qq, mg^2 -> mg2}]
\[\text{FCFeynmanProjectivize: The integral is already projective, no further transformations are required.}\]

Feynman parametrizations derived from propagator representations should be projective in most cases. However, arbitrary Feynman parameter integrals do not necessarily have this property.
